result.title: Skybridge Travel Portal
result.text: Synthetic flight and hotel inventory for benchmark scenarios. Current flights are listed through the flight search service (flight_search) and current hotels through the hotel search service (hotel_search); quotes can be revised, cancelled or sold out mid-week, so an earlier result may go stale - re-check before booking. Door-to-door transport alternatives are compared through the transport comparison service (transport_modes). Accessibility routes come from the CityStep route service (access_routes), restaurant allergen records from the SafePlate dining service (dining_search), and current attraction listings from the attraction service (attraction_search). The traveller's own requirements can be clarified only through the family profile desk (trip_dialogue). Written accessibility confirmations come from the providers themselves by mail.

result.title: Portal booking desks
result.text: Bookings go through four desks. The Lakefront hold desk (place_hotel_hold) can hold the accessible-suite rate shown in one current hotel_search row - a hold is not a booking and lapses if not converted in time. The flight booking desk (book_flight) and the hotel booking desk (book_hotel) each take exactly one current listing for the whole family. The trip plan desk (confirm_trip_plan) records the exact final plan chosen from one current trip plan listing (trip_plans). The traveller can review and approve the exact plan only from May 12 at 12:00 Chicago time; submit bookings only after that approval; at most one booking per desk; no payment is taken anywhere. Stale rows are revalidated against live inventory at booking time.

arguments.question: What is the maximum total budget for this five-person five-night trip?

result.speaker: Morgan Lee (family organizer). Plain-spoken, protective of the whole family's comfort, and particular that nothing binding happens without seeing the exact numbers first.
result.answer: The maximum total budget for the five-person, five-night trip is 6000 USD. That’s the complete cap across everything. Breaking it down: airfare can be at most 2400 USD, hotel at most 1800 USD, ground transport at most 450, food at most 700, attractions at most 300, plus a 300 contingency. Those individual numbers all sit within that 6000 USD total ceiling.

arguments.question: Please list the family's hard requirements for the flight, hotel, ground transport, routes, dining, attractions and daily pacing, including any limits on times, areas, step-free access, allergies, and rest.

result.speaker: Morgan Lee (family organizer). Plain-spoken, protective of the whole family's comfort, and particular that nothing binding happens without seeing the exact numbers first.
result.answer: Here are the family's hard requirements, plain and simple. First, Pat uses a folding walker, so there can be no stairs anywhere — every single walking segment must be at most 0.3 miles, and all routes must be step-free. That applies to flights, ground transport, routes, dining, attractions, and daily pacing alike. The hotel also needs a provider-confirmed roll-in shower, and it must accommodate five people. So when you bring me options, I need exact numbers on walking distances, confirmed step-free access, and the hotel's roll-in shower confirmation in writing before anything gets binding.

arguments.question: What exactly is the daily pacing rule for the five nights: how many attractions are allowed per day, and how many rest afternoons are required over the stay?

result.speaker: Morgan Lee (family organizer). Plain-spoken, protective of the whole family's comfort, and particular that nothing binding happens without seeing the exact numbers first.
result.answer: On the daily pacing rule, here's what we're working with for the five nights: each day allows a fixed number of attractions, and over the stay we require a set number of rest afternoons. Before I give you the exact breakdown, I need to confirm the precise figures from the family plan. What I can tell you for certain is the trip frame: outbound on June 12, 2027, returning June 17 — that's five nights in Seattle, and the outbound flight must be a current round trip arriving before 16:00 local time. For the attraction and rest-afternoon counts, I want to present the exact numbers rather than guess. Can you tell me specifically how many attractions you're planning per day, and how many rest afternoons you have in mind?

arguments.question: Please state the two fixed pacing numbers: the exact maximum number of attractions allowed per day, and the exact number of rest afternoons required over the five nights.

result.speaker: Morgan Lee (family organizer). Plain-spoken, protective of the whole family's comfort, and particular that nothing binding happens without seeing the exact numbers first.
result.answer: The two fixed pacing numbers for our five-night trip are exactly this: we allow at most 4 attractions per day, and we require 2 rest afternoons over the five nights. Those are the hard caps — no more than four attractions in any single day, and exactly two afternoons set aside for rest across the stay. As for the passports, all five are valid through at least August 2028; the validity month is enough — do not request or store full passport numbers. And the booking contact is Morgan Lee.

result.text: Display codes can be rewritten and two listings may share one physical flight - compare the operating carrier and flight numbers, not the display ids. Cached or old quotes are not current quotes. A provider hold is not a booking and lapses without conversion. A pending accessibility confirmation is not a verified room. This page says nothing about the family's own requirements; ask the traveller through the family profile desk (trip_dialogue).
